q1_issues.issue: (Member sk_translate_1 task) is asserted at strength 1.0 even though the text says only that translating is *not* an easy task; the denial is applied to `easy` alone, so the parse positively asserts half of the very predicate nominal the sentence negates.
The gerundive subject "Translating sentences" is reified as an ordinary positive event witness, asserting that a translating eventuality holds rather than predicating of the activity itself.

q2_gaps: gerund / non-finite clause as the subject of a copular clause ("Translating sentences is not an easy task") - Two kinds of clause decides copular vs verbal by the predicate but gives no encoding for an activity-denoting clausal subject

negation over a multi-atom predicate nominal ("is not an easy task") - Negation (copular) says to set strength 0.0 "on the same atom", but an adjective + noun predicate yields two atoms and nothing states which of them take 0.0 (or whether they must be denied jointly as one bundle)
notes: Not fusing "easy task" is right (incidental/evaluative description, not a classifying compound), and the bare-class Theme `sentence` for the non-specific object follows the bare-class-symbol rule.
